CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: breast

1 of 7 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 2 fall below it; 4 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Glycogen (glycoCEST) - breast is not a glycogen-storage organ; no quantified concentration in human breast found; estimated <1 mM, below threshold; [model's own exclusion] Glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST) - cartilage/disc-specific GAG pool; absent in breast parenchyma; [model's own exclusion] myo-inositol - detected in breast HR-MAS but has NO exchangeable protons (0 H_ex), so cannot produce 1H-CEST contrast; [model's own exclusion] Total choline / phosphomonoesters (PME) / phosphodiesters (PDE) - 1H/31P MRS peak groupings of chemically unrelated compounds, not a single molecule or polymer; [model's own exclusion] Glutathione - borderline, ~1-5 mM and diluted below threshold in bulk breast volume; SH exchange outside typical 1H-CEST range; [model's own exclusion] ATP / phosphocreatine as 31P peaks - 31P-only observables, off-target for 1H CEST

Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) — CEST: ✓ detectable (both)

Concentration: 80.00 mM typical (50-150 mM (depends on cellularity; tumor > fibroglandular))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: This is an estimate, not a measured value. Breast fibroglandular tissue is cellular: glandular epithelium plus stroma, with ~12-15% dry mass and ~80% of that dry mass being protein. With ~1000 g protein per L wet tissue (i.e. ~1 g/g), at an average residue mass of ~144 Da this gives roughly 7000 mM residue-equivalent total, but only a fraction is in the mobile, freely-tumbling protein/peptide fraction that APT actually reports (mobile protein ~10-15% of cellular protein by the standard APT model), yielding a typical ~50-150 mM mobile-amide estimate. Tumor cellularity is higher, so tumor amide pool is on the upper end. This is consistent with APT CEST signals being clearly detectable and higher in tumor than fibroglandular tissue in multiple human studies (PMIDs 32574936, 34477453).

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (aliphatic C-H (rNOE) [rnoe]: concentration 50-150 mM, kex fixed at 5 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown); backbone amide NH [amide]: concentration 50-150 mM, kex 15-158 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.67-1.98%, 1.5 T: 1.21-3.54%, 3 T: 0.54-5.35%, 5 T: 0.61-6.10%, 7 T: 0.56-8.18%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • Decisive collision: amide 3.5 ppm vs the creatine amide group (also 3.5 ppm) = 0 Hz at every field, fully merged and indistinguishable from creatine's methylamide peak.
  • So the 3.5 ppm breast 'APT' peak actually contains both protein and creatine amides. rNOE (-3.5 ppm) sits on the broad semisolid MT pool (-2.4 ppm) at all fields - expected, so rNOE must be extracted by fitting, not read off a raw offset. At 0.5-1.5 T the rNOE also blurs with lactate (0.75) and creatine guanidinium (2.0).

Direct water saturation: Both offsets (3.5/-3.5 ppm) are well outside the direct-saturation bandwidth (10.6-31.9 Hz) at every field; no direct-saturation masking of either group.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: Amide kex 65.5 s−1 is borrowed (brain, human in vivo; values 15 and 116 s−1, wide spread); no breast- or protein-specific measurement. rNOE 5 s−1 is a class-level phantom value (PMID 25996515, protein solutions), definitely not a breast in-vivo measurement; rNOE rates depend strongly on macromolecular mobility and temperature. Discount point estimates. The 7 T uncertainty corner (0.56-8.18%) brackets the result, so amide detectability is robust but the point value is not.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 1.070% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 1.920% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Amide is in the slow/intermediate-exchange regime: contrast peaks at low B1 where the pool is partially saturated without spillover into water; raising B1 only broadens the water line and steals contrast via direct saturation, so the optimum sits at 0.5 µT with long Tsat (3000 ms).
    recommended sequence: 2.478% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same slow-exchange physics; peak B1 stays at 0.5 µT with long Tsat as the optimum B1 rises only modestly with B0.
    recommended sequence: 2.819% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At higher B0 the optimal saturation power shifts up (0.75 µT) but Tsat remains long, consistent with a slow-exchanging pool whose contrast is lost to direct water saturation above the optimum.
    recommended sequence: 3.049% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: Most clinical breast APT studies report single-offset MTRasym (PMID 31532006, 31136039), but it is confounded by the overlapping creatine-amide peak and by rNOE/MT. Multi-pool Lorentzian or MTRREX/AREX (PMID 41553443, 35299614) is preferred to separate amide from rNOE and from the creatine amide. Amide is slow/intermediate exchange at moderate B1, so T1-normalized AREX is sound; omega-plot needs >=2 B1 powers.

Potential clinical impact

No verified disease application of this pool's CEST/NOE signal was found. Searched APT/amide proton transfer MRI breast. Rich human + mouse CEST evidence found. No separate non-CEST metabolite-change entry needed (APT is the macromolecular amide pool itself).

Caveats / critique (6 points, 305 words) — 80 mM is high for the free mobile amide pool; APT contrast tracks labile amide protons, not total protein mass, and most amides are H-bonded/crowded in macromol…
  • 80 mM is high for the free mobile amide pool; APT contrast tracks labile amide protons, not total protein mass, and most amides are H-bonded/crowded in macromolecules. The 2.5-3% point estimate is plausibly high, but directionally correct and consistent with multi-percent human breast tumor MTRasym. No breast-specific APT kex or shift is measured; all borrowed from brain/liver.
  • Treat absolute contrast as an estimate. Group classes correct. Backbone amide NH = amide (intermediate exchange) is the right CEST-defining pool; aliphatic C-H = rnoe is correct. One simplification: Agent 2 modeled mobile-protein rNOE as a single -3.5 ppm pool with 7 protons, whereas in vivo it is a broad upfield envelope (1-4 ppm, multi-peak; e.g.
  • PMID 36929814 rat brain homogenates). Acceptable for screening but the rNOE is not one sharp peak. No neglected exchangeable groups. Simulated amide shift 3.5 ppm matches in-vivo breast APT (~3.5 ppm) reported in PMID 31532006 and 31136039. rNOE modeled at -3.5 ppm, a single offset; in vivo mobile-protein rNOE is a broad upfield band rather than one line. None.
  • The backbone amide is the defining CEST pool; rNOE C-H correctly flagged non-exchangeable. verifying_citations: PMID 29111410 (claimed as 'Relayed NOE / rNOE of mobile protons in ex vivo human blood at 7 T.') dropped -- PubMed's actual title is 'The z-spectrum from human blood at 7T.'.
  • no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor n_exchangeable_protons = 1 per mobile amide residue. This is the primary, well-established endogenous CEST target for breast. Concentration is inferred, not directly measured, because APT studies report relative CEST signal rather than absolute mobile-protein mM.
  • [Unsourced reasoning] 1 numeric step(s) rest on an unsourced assumption: 'Only ~10-15% of total protein is in the freely mobile (tumbling) fract'.

Creatine (total) — CEST: ✗ not detectable

Concentration: 10.00 mM typical (5-20 mM)

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: This is an estimate. Creatine (tCr) is a standard, reliably detected metabolite in human breast HR-MAS and is even used as an internal reference in several of these studies (PMIDs 33778749, 23272149, 20101607), indicating it is present at a clearly measurable, multi-mM level. The retrieved abstracts do not give an explicit mM value. Non-muscle soft tissues (liver, kidney) typically contain ~5-15 mM total creatine (Bergmeyer), and breast is comparable, so I estimate ~10 mM typical, range 5-20 mM.

Robustness to input uncertainty: upper-bound only

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (methylamide amide NH [amide]: concentration 5-20 mM, kex 15-158 s−1; guanidinium NH [guanidinium]: concentration 5-20 mM, kex 80-1000 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 0.02-0.14%, 1.5 T: 0.04-0.53%, 3 T: 0.05-0.71%, 5 T: 0.08-0.58%, 7 T: 0.10-0.73%. Threshold 0.5%. The point estimate is below threshold; only the high corner clears it.

Frequency-collision analysis: Creatine amide (3.5) vs APT amide (3.5): 0 Hz at all fields - fully merged, cannot be attributed to creatine specifically. Guanidinium (2.0) is reasonably isolated from the 3.5 amide cluster at 5-7 T (diagnostics flag guanidinium as the best group there) but overlaps lactate hydroxyl (0.75) at 0.5 T (26.6 Hz, within combined linewidth). At 3-7 T the guanidinium is the most cleanly separated creatine peak.

Direct water saturation: At 5-7 T with swept 1.5 µT, direct_sat_bandwidth is 63.9 Hz; guanidinium at 2.0 ppm is 126-168 Hz from water at 3-7 T, just outside the bandwidth - borderline but acceptable. At lower B1 (0.5 µT, 3 T) bandwidth is 21.3 Hz and separation ~126 Hz, comfortably clear. No severe masking.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: Guanidinium kex 575 s−1 borrowed from human calf muscle (3T/7T; 150 and 1000 s−1), not breast; muscle guanidinium kinetics may differ from breast. Amide kex 65.5 s−1 borrowed from brain (class-level, not creatine-specific). No breast-specific measurement. The kex spread (80-1000) brackets the guanidinium contrast (0.08-0.59% at 5 T); discount point estimates.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.085% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.223% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At low field the apparent exchange is slower and the optimum B1 drops to 0.5 µT with long Tsat; guanidinium contrast is still below threshold here (0.30%), so this is not a recommended operating point.
    recommended sequence: 0.302% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=1.5 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Guanidinium is faster (intermediate) exchange, so the optimum B1 rises to 1.5 µT and Tsat shortens to 750 ms - the faster pool peaks at higher B1 before direct-saturation and spillover erode it.
    recommended sequence: 0.384% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1.5 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At 7 T the faster guanidinium optimum stays at 1.5 µT with ~1 s Tsat; contrast reaches 0.48%, the closest to the 0.5% threshold - the only field where creatine guanidinium is borderline-detectable.
    recommended sequence: 0.477% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: Guanidinium is a faster (intermediate) exchanger than amide, favoring higher B1 and AREX/omega-plot (multiple B1) to remove T1/direct-saturation bias; simple 2 ppm MTRasym is used in creatine-CEST brain/muscle papers (PMID 38483851) but is confounded by MT. The 3.5 amide overlap with APT means single-offset MTRasym cannot attribute that peak to creatine - multi-pool Lorentzian or LAREX (PMID 35805925) is required.

Potential clinical impact

No verified disease application of this pool's CEST/NOE signal was found. Searched creatine-weighted CEST and 1H/31P MRS creatine in breast. Only the murine multiparametric CEST study found; 31P MRS does not measure creatine and no 1H-MRS breast creatine reported, so no metabolite-change entry.

Caveats / critique (7 points, 346 words) — 10 mM total creatine in breast is not well supported - creatine/creatine-phosphate CEST is established in brain and muscle, not breast; breast MRS usually repor…
  • 10 mM total creatine in breast is not well supported - creatine/creatine-phosphate CEST is established in brain and muscle, not breast; breast MRS usually reports total creatine as small or negligible. The 10 mM (range 5-20) is an assumption; a lower true value would push the already-marginal guanidinium contrast further below 0.5%. Treat guanidinium detectability as optimistic.
  • Both exchangeable groups caught: guanidinium (1 NH, intermediate) and methylamide amide (1 NH, intermediate) - good. Classes correct. Chemist's ppm guesses (1.4 guanidinium, 3.0 amide) differ from simulated (2.0 and 3.5 ppm).
  • The 2.0 ppm guanidinium is well supported (PMID 26374674, 37036030), but the 3.5 amide is the generic class-level amide value, NOT a measured creatine methylamide - this drives the exact collision with APT below. No neglected protons. Simulated guanidinium shift 2.0 ppm matches in-vivo muscle/brain creatine (2.0-2.4 ppm, PMID 26374674, 37036030). Chemist's 1.4 ppm was a low guess.
  • The 3.5 ppm amide is a class-level amide value, not a creatine-specific measured shift, so the creatine amide vs APT amide identity (0 Hz) may overstate their exact co-location in breast. None. Both the guanidinium NH and the methylamide NH are included; the remaining protons are non-exchangeable C-H.
  • verifying_citations: PMID 26374674 (claimed as 'Creatine guanidinium CEST in human calf muscle in vivo at 7 T with phantoms.') dropped -- PubMed's actual title is 'Relaxation-compensated CEST-MRI at 7\u2009T for mapping of creatine content and pH--preliminary application in human muscle tissue in vivo.'.
  • no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Chemist agent's proposed structure was WRONG and has been replaced with PubChem's verified structure for 'Creatine'. Rejected SMILES: 'CN(C)C(=O)NC1CCNCC1'; PubChem: 'CN(CC(=O)O)C(=N)N'.
  • The exchangeable-proton groups below are still the chemist's own analysis and may have been reasoned from the wrong structure. n_exchangeable_protons 1 (guanidinium; 3H but fast-exchanging). Creatine has a strong guanidinium/amine CEST signal around 3 ppm. Lactate — CEST: ✗ not detectable

Concentration: 15.00 mM typical (5-30 mM (Warburg effect, higher in tumor))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: This is an estimate. Lactate is quantified by HR-MAS in human breast biopsies (PMIDs 21823183, 20101607) and is lower in patients with long-term survival, consistent with it being a measurable multi-mM metabolite in tumor. The retrieved abstracts give no explicit mM value. Breast tumors exhibit the Warburg effect (aerobic glycolysis) so lactate is elevated; I estimate ~15 mM typical in tumor, range 5-30 mM, lower in normal breast.

Frequency-collision analysis: At 0.5 T the 0.75 ppm OH is within combined linewidth of APT amide (58.5 Hz), creatine guanidinium (26.6 Hz), creatine amide, and rNOE - heavily congested and unresolvable. By 5-7 T separation from the 3.5 amide cluster and 2.0 guanidinium opens up (670-939 Hz), so the residual collision is mainly with the broad MT pool, as flagged. Low field is the worst case for lactate.

Direct water saturation: The OH at 0.75 ppm is close to water (~15 Hz at 0.5 T, just outside the 4.3 Hz bandwidth). At higher B1 the bandwidth grows (42.6 Hz at 7 T) while the offset in Hz also grows, so it stays marginally clear. The bigger issue is fast exchange merging the pool toward water rather than direct-saturation masking per se.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: Lactate OH kex 600 s−1 is BORROWED from myo-inositol hydroxyl (human brain, 7T, PMID 20951217), not from lactate - a cross-metabolite borrow. The 0.75 ppm shift comes from a phantom/cadaver/in-vivo leg study (PMID 35645392). In-vivo lactate OH exchange can differ from inositol's and from phantom values (pH, T, crowding). Lower confidence in the point estimate; even the upper 7 T corner (0.67%) only marginally approaches threshold.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.025% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.049% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=500 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.115% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.223% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.337% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

Glutamate — CEST: ? unknown (not simulated)

Concentration: 15.00 mM typical (5-30 mM (higher in glutaminolytic tumors such as TNBC)) animal evidence only

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: This is an estimate. PMID 30072394 is the key anchor: a 2-day glutaminase inhibitor (CB-839) reduced tumor glutamate by 1.5 mmol/L, and the authors calibrated the GluCEST signal against tissue glutamate concentration, implying the total tumor glutamate pool is on the multi-mM order (the change of 1.5 mmol/L is a substantial fraction of the pool). For human breast tumors with active glutaminolysis (TNBC) I estimate ~15 mM typical, range 5-30 mM; normal breast is lower (free pool <1-2 mM but total including GSH-linked glutamate higher). The quantitative anchor is from a mouse xenograft, so this is flagged animal_evidence_only for the number, with human qualitative support from the metabolomics review (PMID 39791706).

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — coronal; centred at the mid-axillary / nipple level so the slab contains the fibroglandular breast, overlying subcutaneous fat, and the posterior pectoral muscle in one FOV

Why this scan:

  • A coronal 3 T slab through the breast simultaneously contains fibroglandular tissue (dense, ~80 mM mobile amide), the overlying subcutaneous fat, the interlobular breast adipose, and the posterior pectoral muscle. One saturation train is applied to all.
  • A genuine APT effect at +3.5 ppm must scale with the mobile amide pool, which differs markedly across these tissues (glandular >> muscle > adipose >> fat). Generic background MT/NOE at a fixed offset is roughly similar across ROIs, so an offset-dependent contrast that tracks these known protein-density differences identifies the effect as real APT exchange rather than background.
  • The rNOE side-chain mirror at -3.5 ppm is sampled to confirm the upfield pool is the same mobile-protein source.
ROIWhere it is drawnRole
Breast fibroglandular tissue target tissueDrawn over the dense glandular/fibrous portion of the breast on the coronal slab, away from gross fat lobules and any mass.TARGET tissue; highest mobile-amine/protein density in the FOV.
Subcutaneous fatThe uniform fat layer immediately anterior to the glandular tissue, drawn in a homogeneous region with no glandular interspersed.Comparison tissue with the lowest protein/water; tabulated in pipeline as subcutaneous fat.
Breast adipose tissueThe lobular/interlobular fat within the breast parenchyma, drawn as a homogeneous fatty region separate from dense glandular tissue.Comparison tissue with low protein; tabulated in pipeline as breast adipose tissue.
Pectoral muscleThe pectoralis major posterior to the breast on the same coronal slab, drawn in the muscle belly away from the chest wall interface.Comparison muscle with moderate protein; tabulated in pipeline (paraspinal/muscle muscle) for tabulated water T1/T2/MT.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed rectangular train (duty-cycled, not CW), B1=0.5 µT, 25 pulses × 100 ms (interpulse delay 20 ms, duty cycle 83.3%), total Tsat=3000 ms, TR=3500 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model): 0.5 µT at 83% duty over a ~3 s window and ~12 cm breast slab is well below the 0.9-2 µT used in clinical breast APT-CEST (PMID 34477453) and far under the 2 W/kg whole-body limit; the short 3 s saturation window keeps cumulative SAR low.

Compromise rationale: Only APT is an active candidate, so 0.5 µT / 3 s targets its ~3.5 ppm amide peak near the physicist's 3 T optimum (intermediate exchange). No cross-metabolite conflict. The rNOE side-chain (~-3.5 ppm) is sampled passively as the mirror offset. A higher B1 (>=2 µT) would oversaturate the water pool and blur APT/MT separation, so low-power 0.5 µT is preferred for a differential concentration-driven readout. 25 pulses over 3 s (83% duty) gives near-continuous saturation of the amide pool.

Fat suppression: Dual-echo water-fat separation plus a SPIR/SPAIR prepulse, combined with the residual-fat-normalization approach of PMID 31532006. Breast is 50-80% fat; uncorrected fat corrupts Z-spectrum normalization and the MTRasym denominator, so robust fat handling is mandatory for this anatomy.

Motion mitigation: Free-breathing with a navigator or short breath-hold per slab; the breast is relatively insensitive to respiration versus the abdomen. Cap the full multi-offset 3D slab at ~6-8 min. No cardiac gating (not cardiac), no CSF-pulsation concern.

Slice coverage: Coronal 3D slab, ~30 slices x 3 mm covering both breasts from skin surface to chest wall, centred at the mid-axillary/nipple level, FOV ~28 cm x 24 cm, so that glandular tissue, overlying subcutaneous fat, interlobular breast adipose, and pectoral muscle all fall within one slab.

Structures in FOV: Breast fibroglandular tissue, Subcutaneous fat, Breast adipose tissue, Pectoral muscle, chest wall / skin

Z-spectrum sampling offsets:

  • -8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference
  • -3.50 ppm: rNOE side-chain (mobile protein), mirror of APT for MTRasym
  • -1.90 ppm: symmetric reference for MTRasym
  • +0.00 ppm: water (0 ppm), normalization reference
  • +1.90 ppm: symmetric reference for MTRasym
  • +3.50 ppm: APT (mobile protein/peptide amide pool)
  • +3.50 ppm: B0-correction (WASSR) reference point
  • +8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference

Differential analysis plan:

  • ROI-average the Z-spectra in each of the four ROIs, compute MTRasym at +3.5 ppm (and a Lorentzian-difference APT peak) after B0 (WASSR) and B1 correction and fat-signal normalization. At +3.5 ppm, a true APT contribution must rank glandular (highest) > muscle > breast adipose > subcutaneous fat, tracking the derived amide concentrations (80 > 45 > 10 > 4 mM).
  • Confirming pattern: offset-dependent amide peak that follows this concentration ranking while the -3.5 ppm rNOE mirror tracks the same pool. Inconclusive pattern: similar amplitude across ROIs at +3.5 ppm (background MT/NOE), a peak ranking that contradicts the concentration order, or a dominant 0-ppm/MT artefact.

Not actively targeted: Creatine (total), Lactate, Glycine, Taurine, Glutamate, and Phosphocholine were not actively designed around: the physicist agent reported low/no simulated with-vs-without contrast at any field strength, and their shifts (e.g. lactate ~1.3 ppm, creatine ~3.0 ppm) overlap the APT region so a single compromise protocol targeting APT at 3.5 ppm does not isolate them.

Caveats:

  • Real limits: (1) partial volume - glandular and fat lobules interdigitate at mm scale, so ROIs near fat-glandular borders mix signals (2) B0/B1 inhomogeneity across the fat-muscle-water slab persists even after WASSR/B1 correction, and fat signal distorts normalization (PMID 31532006) (3) susceptibility at the chest wall/bone interface can distort offsets
  • (4) one compromise B1/Tsat (0.5 µT / 3 s) is optimal for APT only and cannot simultaneously optimize every excluded metabolite (5) derived comparison concentrations are estimates from protein/water composition, not direct measurements, so the expected ROI ranking carries uncertainty.
